chunks.text: Aventro Motors: How to Change a Tyre Changing a flat tyre is a basic and essential automotive skill for every Aventro Motor car owner. This guide will walk you through: • Steps to change a tyre • Where the spare tyre and toolkit is found in all Aventro models • General tips and safety instructions Where to Find the Spare Tyre & Toolkit in Aventro Models Model Type Common Location of Spare Tyre & Toolkit Hatchback Under the boot floor in the rear compartment Sedan Under the boot floor in the trunk SUV Under the boot floor or mounted underneath the rear of the car (All Models) Toolkit is usually secured next to the spare tyre or inside a side panel of the boot/trunk Note: All variants (Petrol/Diesel/Electric/Hybrid) follow the same compart- ment arrangement. Steps to Change a Tyre 1. Park Safely • Pull over to a safe, flat location away from traﬀic. • Turn on your hazard lights. • Apply the handbrake. • Place wheel wedges/blocks (if available) to prevent vehicle movement. 2. Gather Tools You will need: - Spare tyre (found as per table above) - Jack (usually in toolkit) - Lug wrench (in toolkit) - Wheel wedges/blocks (optional) - Vehicle owner’s manual (for reference) 3. Remove the Wheel Cover/Hubcap • If your wheel has a cover, use the flat end of the wrench or the provided lever to gently pry it off. 1

chunks.text: 4. Loosen the Lug Nuts • Use the lug wrench to turn the lug nuts counter-clockwise. • Loosen them slightly – do not remove fully at this stage. 5. Lift the Vehicle with the Jack • Position the jack under the jacking point nearest to the flat tyre. Refer to your owner’s manual for the exact point. • Raise the vehicle until the flat tyre is about 6 inches above the ground. 6. Remove the Lug Nuts and Tyre • Unscrew the lug nuts completely. • Remove the flat tyre and set it aside. 7. Mount the Spare Tyre • Line up the holes and push the spare onto the hub. • Replace the lug nuts and tighten them by hand. 8. Lower the Vehicle • Carefully lower the car with the jack until the tyre touches the ground firmly. • Remove the jack. 9. Tighten the Lug Nuts • Use the lug wrench to tighten the lug nuts in a star pattern to ensure even pressure. 10. Replace the Hubcap or Wheel Cover (if applicable) • Place the hubcap back onto the wheel. 11. Stow Equipment • Put the flat tyre, jack, and tools back in their compartments. • Double check everything is secure. Safety & Tips • Never change a tyre on a slope or close to traﬀic. • Use hazard warning triangle if available. • After installation, drive slowly and get the spare tyre pressure checked at the nearest Aventro Service Center. 2

Adaptive Cruise Control (ACC): What is it & How Does it Work? Overview Adaptive Cruise Control (ACC) is an advanced driver assistance system (ADAS) designed to automatically adjust a vehicle’s cruising speed to maintain a safe following distance from vehicles ahead. It’s an evolution of traditional cruise control, offering greater safety, comfort, and convenience—especially in highway and stop-and-go traﬀic scenarios. What is Adaptive Cruise Control? • Traditional Cruise Control: Maintains a set vehicle speed as chosen by the driver. • Adaptive Cruise Control: Uses sensors to detect vehicles ahead and can increase, decrease, or maintain speed based on traﬀic conditions. Key Functions 1. Automatic Speed Regulation Keeps the car traveling at a set speed until it detects a slower-moving vehicle in its path. 2. Distance Monitoring & Maintenance Constantly monitors the distance to the vehicle in front and adjusts speed to maintain a safe, pre-set gap. 3. Automatic Braking and Acceleration Decelerates when a slower vehicle is detected, and speeds back up to the original set speed when the lane clears. 4. Stop & Go Functionality (in advanced systems) In heavy traﬀic, can bring the car to a complete stop and resume motion as traﬀic moves. How Does Adaptive Cruise Control Work? Main Components • Radar Sensors: Typically mounted in the grille or front bumper to detect vehicles ahead and measure their speed and distance. • Lidar Sensors or Cameras: Used in some systems for enhanced object detection and lane tracking. 1

• ECU (Electronic Control Unit): Processes sensor data and commands the throttle and brakes as needed. Working Principle 1. Activation The driver activates ACC and sets a desired speed and following distance (often via steering wheel controls). 2. Monitoring The system continuously scans the road ahead using radar, lidar, and/or cameras. 3. Detection • If the road ahead is clear, ACC maintains the set speed. • If a slower vehicle is detected within the pre-set following distance, ACC automatically reduces vehicle speed by controlling throttle and brakes. 4. Control • If the vehicle ahead speeds up, ACC accelerates (up to the set speed limit). • If the vehicle ahead slows down or stops, ACC decelerates and—if equipped with stop & go—can bring the car to a halt. 5. Resuming The system accelerates back to the set speed once the lane ahead is clear. Example Scenario • You set ACC to 100 km/h and the following distance to 2 seconds. • A car merges ahead traveling at 80 km/h. • ACC detects the vehicle and smoothly reduces your speed to maintain a safe gap. • When the lane ahead is clear, ACC returns your car to 100 km/h. Advantages • Safety: Reduces risk of rear-end collisions. • Convenience: Less driver fatigue on long trips and in traﬀic jams. • Eﬀiciency: Optimized speed and braking can improve fuel economy. Limitations • Sensor Limitations: May be affected by weather conditions, dirt, or obstructions. 2

• Not a Substitute for Attention: The driver must remain alert and ready to take control at all times. Terminology • ACC: Adaptive Cruise Control • ADAS: Advanced Driver Assistance Systems Summary Table Feature Traditional Cruise Control Adaptive Cruise Control Maintains Set Speed Yes Yes Senses Vehicles Ahead No Yes Adjusts Following Gap No Yes Automatic Braking No Yes Resumes after Stopping No In advanced ACC References • NHTSA: Adaptive Cruise Control • SAE International: ADAS Features Guide • Vehicle Owner’s Manuals (Various Manufacturers) 3

Adjusting the Seat Positions in Aventro Motors Vehicles Overview Proper seat adjustment is essential for driving comfort, safety, and visibility. Aventro Motors vehicles are equipped with manual and/or electronic seat ad- justment controls, depending on the model and trim. This guide walks you through adjusting your seat position for the safest and most comfortable driv- ing experience. Steps for Adjusting the Seat Positions 1. Adjusting the Seat Distance from the Pedals • Locate the seat adjustment lever under the front edge of the seat. • Pull the lever up to unlock the seat. • Slide the seat forward or backward until your feet reach the pedals com- fortably while keeping a slight bend at your knees. • Release the lever to lock the seat in position. • Gently rock the seat to ensure it is securely locked. 2. Adjusting the Seat Height (if equipped) • Locate the seat height adjustment lever or electronic control (usually on the side of the seat). • For manual systems, pump the lever up or down. • For electronic systems, use the corresponding switch to raise or lower the seat. • Adjust until you have a clear view over the steering wheel and dashboard, with adequate headspace. 3. Adjusting the Seat Backrest Angle • Find the seat backrest adjustment lever or rotary knob at the side of the seat. • Lean forward slightly and pull or rotate the control to release the backrest. • Adjust the backrest angle so you are sitting upright, with your shoulders touching the seatback. • The ideal angle is slightly reclined for comfort, but never more than 30° from upright. • Ensure the backrest is firmly locked in position before driving. 4. Adjusting the Headrest • Hold both sides of the headrest. 1

• Press the adjustment button (usually at the base) and move the headrest up or down. • The top of the headrest should be level with the top of your head. • The headrest should be as close to the back of your head as possible for optimal safety. 5. Adjusting the Lumbar Support (if equipped) • Use the lumbar support lever, dial, or electronic switch (side of seatback). • Increase or decrease support as needed for comfort and spine alignment. • Proper lumbar support helps reduce fatigue on long drives. Tips for Safe Seat Adjustment • Adjust your seat before starting the engine and while the car is stationary. • Ensure all adjustments are firmly locked in place before driving. • The distance between your chest and the steering wheel should be at least 25 cm (10 inches). • Adjust the steering wheel if required, for optimal hand positioning. • All passengers should also adjust their seats and headrests. Troubleshooting Issue Possible Solution Seat not moving Check for obstructions under the seat. Electronic controls not working Check vehicle battery or fuses. Seat does not lock in place Re-engage lever or consult service center. Headrest stuck Press and hold release button firmly. Need Assistance? For in-depth troubleshooting or if you experience issues with seat adjustment mechanisms, contact your nearest Aventro Service Center or call Aventro Motors Customer Support at +91 124 1234567. Drive safe, drive smart with Aventro! 2

Adjusting the Steering Wheel Proper steering wheel adjustment is essential for comfortable and safe driving. Follow these steps to adjust your steering wheel for an optimal driving position. Why Adjust the Steering Wheel? • Comfort: Reduces fatigue during long drives. • Control: Ensures effective steering and better handling. • Safety: Ensures clear view of the instrument cluster and optimal airbag positioning. Types of Steering Wheel Adjustments Most Aventro Motors vehicles come with either or both of the following: • Tilt Adjustment: Allows the wheel to move up and down. • Telescopic Adjustment: Allows the wheel to move closer or farther from the driver. Step-by-Step Guide 1. Park the Vehicle Safely • Ensure the vehicle is on a flat surface and engage the parking brake. • Turn off the engine for safety. 2. Locate the Adjustment Lever • Look for the steering adjustment lever beneath or on the side of the steer- ing column, usually beneath the wheel. 3. Release the Lever • Pull (or push, depending on the model) the adjustment lever to unlock the steering wheel movement. 4. Adjust the Steering Wheel • Tilt: Move the wheel up or down to a comfortable height. • Telescopic: Pull the wheel towards you or push it away to set a comfort- able distance. • The steering wheel should not obstruct your view of the gauges. 1

5. Lock the Steering Wheel Position • Once set, firmly push the adjustment lever back to the locked position. 6. Check Positioning • With your back against the seat, extend your arms and rest your wrists on top of the wheel; your elbows should be slightly bent. • Ensure there is at least 25 cm (10 inches) between your chest and the wheel (important for airbag safety). • Confirm that all indicator lights and gauges are fully visible. Tips • Adjust your seat first before the steering wheel. • If your vehicle has a heated steering wheel or steering wheel memory set- tings, consult your owner’s manual for additional features. • Never adjust the steering wheel while driving. Troubleshooting • Stuck Lever: Check for obstructions under/around the lever or consult your nearest Aventro Service Center. • Loose Wheel: Ensure the lever is locked; if the wheel remains loose, have it inspected by a professional. For Further Assistance If you encounter issues or need help with adjustments, visit your nearest Aventro Service Center or contact Aventro Motors Support: • Email: info@aventromotors.com • Phone: +91 124 1234567 Drive safely and comfortably! 2

chunks.text: Advice for Pregnant Women While in a Car Traveling by car is common during pregnancy, but it’s important to prioritize safety and comfort for both mother and baby. Here’s a quick guide with essential advice: 1. Always Wear Your Seat Belt Properly • Three-Point Seat Belt: Use both lap and shoulder belts. • Lap Belt: Position it under the belly, low on the hips, and across the upper thighs. It should never go across your stomach. • Shoulder Belt: Place it between the breasts and to the side of your belly. • Never Place Belt Behind Back or Under Arm: This reduces its effectiveness and can be dangerous. 2. Adjust Your Seat for Maximum Comfort and Safety • Sit Upright: Maintain a good posture—back straight, shoulders relaxed. • Distance from Steering Wheel/Airbag: Adjust the seat so you’re as far from the dashboard/steering wheel as possible, but still able to drive comfortably. • Tilt Steering Wheel Upwards: If possible, angle the steering wheel towards your chest, not your belly. 3. Take Frequent Breaks for Long Journeys • Every 60-90 Minutes: Stop and get out to stretch legs and walk a little. This improves circulation and reduces risk of blood clots. • Hydrate and Snack: Drink plenty of water and eat light snacks to avoid dehydration and low blood sugar. 4. Manage Nausea and Discomfort • Travel During Cooler Hours: Early morning or evening can help avoid heat and traﬀic. • Fresh Air: Crack a window or use air conditioning for ventilation. • Motion Sickness: Bring ginger candies, anti-nausea wristbands, or other remedies advised by your doctor. 1

Aventro Motors Guide: Connecting Smartwatch Connectivity, Works with Alexa, and CarPlay Welcome to your Aventro vehicle’s connected features guide! This document explains how to connect and use: - Smartwatch Connectivity - Works with Alexa - Apple CarPlay Below, you’ll find step-by-step setup instructions and troubleshooting tips for each feature. 1. Smartwatch Connectivity Overview Smartwatch connectivity allows you to interact with select vehicle functions directly from your smartwatch. This may include lock/unlock, remote start, finding your car, and vehicle health reports. Compatible Smartwatches • Apple Watch (watchOS 6 and above) • Android Wear OS Watches (Wear OS 2 and above) • Samsung Galaxy Watches (Tizen 4 and above) Steps to Connect A. Install the Aventro Connect App 1. On your smartphone, download the Aventro Connect app from Google Play Store or Apple App Store. 2. Create or log into your Aventro account. B. Pair Your Smartwatch 1. Ensure your smartwatch is paired with your smartphone via Bluetooth and both are connected to the Internet. 2. On your watch, open the relevant app store (Apple Watch App Store, Google Play for Wear OS, or Galaxy Store). 3. Search for Aventro Connect and install it. 4. Open the app on your smartwatch. You may be prompted to sign in with your Aventro account or grant permissions. 5. On your smartphone’s Aventro Connect app, go to Settings > Device Con- nections > Add Smartwatch. 6. Follow on-screen instructions to authorize and link the smartwatch. 1

C. Using Smartwatch Features • Lock/Unlock: Tap the respective button in the app. • Remote Start: Press and hold the remote start icon in the app. • Find My Car: View your vehicle’s last parked location. Troubleshooting • Make sure Bluetooth is enabled on both watch and phone. • Both devices must be within range. • Both devices must have an internet connection. 2. Works with Alexa Overview Control your Aventro car using Alexa-enabled devices and voice commands: lock/unlock car, remote start, check fuel/battery status, etc. Prerequisites • Alexa-enabled device (Echo Dot, Echo Show, Amazon App) • Aventro Connect account • Vehicle registered on Aventro Connect app Steps to Connect 1. On your smartphone, open the Amazon Alexa app. 2. Tap the menu and select Skills & Games. 3. Search for Aventro Motors (Aventro Connect Skill). 4. Tap Enable. 5. Log in with your Aventro Connect account to link it. 6. Grant requested permissions (vehicle control, location, etc.). Example Voice Commands • “Alexa, ask Aventro to start my car.” • “Alexa, ask Aventro if my car is locked.” • “Alexa, ask Aventro how much battery my Aero has left.” Troubleshooting • Ensure car has active Internet connectivity (SIM/eSIM). • User permissions in Aventro Connect app must be up to date. • If unresponsive, try disabling and re-enabling the Aventro skill in the Alexa app. 2

3. Apple CarPlay Overview Apple CarPlay seamlessly integrates your iPhone with your Aventro vehicle’s infotainment system. Use Maps, Music, Calls, and Messages hands-free. Prerequisites • iPhone 6 or newer (iOS 13 or above) • Genuine Apple Lightning cable or wireless pairing (in supported models) Steps to Connect A. Wired CarPlay Connection 1. Start your car and turn on the infotainment system. 2. Plug your iPhone into the car’s USB port with a genuine Apple Lightning cable. 3. CarPlay prompt will appear on your infotainment display. Tap Allow on your iPhone if asked. B. Wireless CarPlay (If Supported) 1. Enable both Bluetooth and Wi-Fi on your iPhone. 2. On the car’s infotainment display, go to Settings > Apple CarPlay > Pair New Device. 3. On your iPhone, go to Settings > General > CarPlay and select your Aventro car. 4. Follow on-screen instructions to pair wirelessly. Common CarPlay Features • Voice: Press and hold the steering wheel’s voice button for Siri. • Maps: Use Apple Maps, Google Maps, Waze, etc. • Messages: Listen and respond hands-free. • Music & Audio: Apple Music, Spotify, Podcasts, etc. Troubleshooting • Restart your iPhone and the infotainment system if CarPlay won’t con- nect. • Use only Apple-certified cables for wired connections. • Make sure your Aventro model supports wireless CarPlay if attempting wireless. 3

Whether you drive a petrol, diesel, hybrid, or electric car from Aventro Mo- tors, the following practices will help you get the most out of every journey. 1. Check Tyre Pressure • Maintain Proper Pressure: Under-inflated tyres increase rolling resis- tance and decrease mileage. • Check Regularly: Inspect tyre pressure at least once a month and before long trips. 3. Drive Smoothly • Avoid Sudden Acceleration or Braking: Rapid changes waste fuel and energy. • Use Gentle Throttle Inputs: Gradual acceleration and deceleration help maximize eﬀiciency. 4. Limit Idling • Turn Off Engine at Long Stops: Idling consumes fuel needlessly in petrol/diesel vehicles. • Use Start-Stop Feature If Equipped: Many Aventro models have this for additional savings. 5. Reduce Excess Weight • Remove Unnecessary Items: Extra load in the boot or cabin means more work for your engine. • Avoid Unused Racks: Roof boxes or roof racks can reduce aerodynamic eﬀiciency. 1

chunks.text: Best Ways to Use Your Car AC in All Seasons For Aventro Motors Car Owners Your vehicle’s air conditioning (AC) system is vital for comfort and safety throughout the year. Whether it’s cooling in summer, defogging in monsoon, or maintaining a pleasant environment in winter, knowing how to use the AC eﬀiciently will extend system life and enhance your driving experience. Here’s a guide to making the most of your AC system during every season. Summer: Beat the Heat 1. Ventilate First - Before switching on the AC, roll down the windows and drive for a couple of minutes to expel hot air. - This makes the cabin cool down faster. 2. Use Recirculation Mode - Turn on the AC and set it to “recirculate” once the cabin is cool. - This prevents hot outside air from entering, making the system more effective. 3. Set the Right Temperature - Avoid setting the thermostat to the lowest setting. 22-24°C (72-75°F) is usually comfortable and easier on the compressor. 4. Regular Maintenance - Clean or replace the cabin air filter. - Get your AC system inspected and refrigerant topped up at an Aventro Service Center before summer starts. Monsoon: Fight Humidity and Fog 1. Use AC for Defogging - Turn on the AC with the blower directed at the windshield to quickly clear fog. - Use the “fresh air” mode for a few minutes to reduce internal humidity. 2. Don’t Use Recirculate Mode Continuously - Constant recirculation during rains may increase humidity inside, causing more fogging. 3. Keep Windows Closed - Prevent water and more humidity from entering the cabin. 1

chunks.text: Best Ways to Use Your headlamps Based on Road, Traﬀic, and Climate Driving conditions in India can vary dramatically depending on loca- tion, weather, and traﬀic density. Your headlamps (often referred to as headlights)—play a crucial role not only for your visibility but for the safety of everyone on the road. This guide from Aventro Motors outlines the best practices for using your headlamps based on distinct road, traﬀic, and climate scenarios. 1. Urban Roads with Heavy Traﬀic • Use low beam: High beams can dazzle oncoming drivers and should be avoided in city traﬀic. • Turn on your headlamps in the evening/low light: Even if street lights are present, using your headlamps enhances visibility. • Hazards & signal lights: Use these for extra safety during sudden traﬀic halts or in bumper-to-bumper situations. 2. Rural Roads & Highways • Switch to high beam on poorly lit or empty stretches: Offers extended visibility where street lighting is absent. • Dip your beam for oncoming vehicles: Always shift back to low beam to avoid blinding other drivers. • Check for road signs: Many rural roads feature animal crossings or sharp curves—reduce speed and use dipped beams. 3. Foggy or Rainy Weather • Always use low beam: High beams reflect off fog or rain, worsening visibility. • Activate fog lamps if available: These cut through the mist close to the road. • Use hazard lights only when stationary on road shoulder: Do not use hazards while driving as it confuses other road users. • Reduce speed and increase distance: Wet roads mean longer stopping distances. 1

Twilight/Dawn and Overcast Days • Turn on your headlamps even if it’s not dark: Light contrast is low and reduces overall visibility. • Switch on tail lamps as well: Make sure drivers behind you can see your vehicle. 6. Hilly and Winding Roads • Always use dipper at turns and blind spots: Alert oncoming vehicles of your presence. • High beam for long stretches at night: But revert to low beam for sharp turns or when climbing gradients. 7. Night Driving • Regularly alternate between high and low beam: Use high for extended visibility and low when another vehicle is near. • Avoid using only parking lights: These are not suﬀicient for visibility or indication. 8. Snowy or Icy Conditions (Himalayan or North-Indian states) • Use low beam: Snow reflects light, causing glare. • Keep headlamps clear of snow/ice: Visibility is severely reduced oth- erwise. • Drive cautiously: Traction and braking are affected. 2

chunks.text: How to Handle “Engine Won’t Start” Issue When your Aventro vehicle’s engine refuses to start, it can be frustrating. Use this step-by-step guide to help diagnose and resolve the problem, or to gather information before contacting an Aventro Service Center. 1. Check the Basics • Gear Position: Ensure the car is in ‘Park’ (automatic) or ‘Neutral’ (man- ual). • Steering Lock: Gently turn the steering wheel while turning the key if steering is locked. • Key/Start Button: Switch ignition off and retry. For push-button start, press brake/clutch while starting. 2. Battery Check • Symptoms: No lights/display, slow/absent cranking sounds, clicking noise. • Actions: – Inspect dashboard for dim or no lights. – Try using headlights or infotainment; if dim or off, battery may be the culprit. – If available, try jump-starting with a healthy battery. – For Electric variants: Ensure Battery Pack has adequate charge. Lane Keeping Assist System (LKAS): Overview & Functionality What is Lane Keeping Assist System (LKAS)? Lane Keeping Assist System (LKAS) is an advanced driver assistance system (ADAS) designed to enhance road safety by helping drivers keep their vehicles within marked lane boundaries. LKAS is commonly found in modern vehicles and acts as a semi-autonomous feature, working alongside the driver to prevent unintentional lane departure. Why is LKAS Important? • Reduces Accidents: Lane departures are a major cause of road acci- dents, especially due to driver drowsiness, distraction, or inattention. • Enhances Safety: By consistently monitoring the vehicle’s position, LKAS can help avoid unintended drift into adjacent lanes. • Supports the Driver: LKAS provides gentle steering inputs or alerts, acting as a backup to human oversight. How Does Lane Keeping Assist System Work? 1. Sensing the Lane • Cameras: Typically, a forward-facing camera mounted near the rear-view mirror scans the road ahead for lane markings (white/yellow lines). • Sensors: Some advanced systems use a combination of cameras, LIDAR, or radar to enhance accuracy in different lighting and weather conditions. 2. Processing the Image • The camera/system detects lane boundaries by analyzing road markings in real-time. • On-board computers determine if the vehicle is unintentionally veering out of its lane. 3. Warning the Driver • If the vehicle starts drifting toward a lane marking without indicating (using a turn signal), the system may give audible or visual warnings (e.g., a beep, steering wheel vibration, or dashboard alert). 1

4. Active Assistance • If the driver doesn’t respond to the warnings, LKAS can automatically provide gentle steering input to guide the car back toward the center of the lane. • Some systems may also use selective braking on one side of the vehicle to assist in correcting the course. Key Features • Automatic Steering Correction: Minor, smooth counter-steering to stay centered in the lane. • Customizable Sensitivity: Most systems allow drivers to adjust the responsiveness or can be switched off. • Integrated with Other Systems: Often works alongside Lane Depar- ture Warning (LDW) and Adaptive Cruise Control (ACC). Limitations & Considerations • Reliant on Lane Markings: LKAS requires clear, visible lane lines; performance may degrade in poor weather, faded markings, or during road construction. • Not a Substitute for Attention: LKAS assists, but the driver must keep hands on the wheel and remain attentive at all times. • May Not Operate at All Speeds: Some systems only work above certain speeds (e.g., above 60 km/h). Typical LKAS Workflow 1. Vehicle Camera Detects Lane 2. Control Unit Monitors Position Relative to Lane Marks 3. If Drift Detected: System Alerts Driver 4. If No Response: System Gently Steers Vehicle Back to Lane Center Conclusion Lane Keeping Assist System is a valuable safety technology that helps prevent unintentional lane departures, reducing the risk of side-swipe collisions and road departure accidents. While it offers significant safety benefits, it is not an au- tonomous driving system—driver vigilance and control remain essential. 2
References/For More Information - NHTSA on Lane Assistance Features - IIHS: Lane Departure Prevention 3

Before You Start the Car □Ensure you are well-rested and not under the influence of alcohol, drugs, or strong medication. □Check weather and road conditions. □Perform a quick walk-around inspection of the car: □Tire condition and pressure □All lights functioning (headlights, brake lights, indicators) □No visible leaks or loose parts □Adjust your seat, headrest, and mirrors for comfort and proper view. □Fasten your seat belt and ensure all passengers are buckled up. □Check that all doors are properly closed and locked. □Clear the windshield and mirrors of obstructions/dirt. □Secure any loose items in the vehicle. 2. Starting the Car □Ensure the gear is in neutral/park. □Press the brake pedal before starting. □Check dashboard warning lights after ignition. □Familiarize yourself with the location of controls (wipers, headlights, horn, indicators, hazard lights). 3. While Driving □Obey all speed limits and traﬀic rules. □Keep a safe following distance (3-second rule in good conditions). □Use indicators when changing lanes or turning. □Observe and obey all road signs and signals. □Avoid distractions: □Do not use mobile phones unless hands-free. □Avoid eating, drinking, or reaching for objects while driving. □Stay focused, alert, and anticipate actions of other drivers. □Use headlights in low light, rain, or fog. □Continuously check rear-view and side mirrors. □Yield to pedestrians and emergency vehicles. 1

Traction Control What is Traction Control? Traction Control is a vehicle safety feature designed to prevent the loss of traction (grip) of the driven road wheels, which can occur during acceleration. By detecting when one or more wheels are slipping, the system automatically applies the brakes or reduces engine power to maintain optimal grip, especially on slippery surfaces. How Does Traction Control Work? Traction control systems are usually integrated with a car’s anti-lock braking system (ABS) and electronic stability control (ESC). The basic operation in- volves: 1. Sensors detect when a wheel is spinning faster than others (indicating loss of traction). 2. Electronic Control Unit (ECU) receives data from sensors and deter- mines the appropriate intervention. 3. Intervention: • Braking: The system applies brakes to the slipping wheel(s). • Engine Control: The ECU may reduce engine power or throttle input to minimize wheel spin. Key Components • Wheel Speed Sensors: Monitor the rotational speed of each wheel. • ECU (Electronic Control Unit): Processes sensor data and manages interventions. • Braking Mechanism: Engages individual brakes as needed. • Throttle Control (in advanced systems): Modulates engine power. Benefits of Traction Control • Improved Safety: Helps maintain control during acceleration on wet, icy, or loose surfaces. • Reduced Wheel Spin: Minimizes tire wear and prevents excessive wheel spin. • Enhanced Stability: Works in tandem with ABS and ESC for overall vehicle stability. 1

When Does Traction Control Activate? • Accelerating quickly on wet, icy, sandy, or gravelly surfaces. • When one or more wheels begin to slip or lose contact with the road. • During sharp turns, especially in low-traction conditions. Limitations of Traction Control • Cannot increase tire traction: Only manages existing traction without creating more. • Limited usefulness on all surfaces: May not be as effective on ex- tremely slippery or uneven terrains. • Not a substitute for safe driving practices: Drivers should still use caution in poor conditions. Traction Control in Aventro Motors Cars Most modern vehicles, including Aventro Motors models across Hatchback, Sedan, and SUV variants, are equipped with traction control as standard or optional, especially in ZX or higher trim levels. This is part of Aventro’s commitment to vehicle safety and performance under varied driving conditions. Traction Control Indicator Light The dashboard display will often include a traction control symbol: - Illumi- nates briefly when system is engaged or if road conditions are slip- pery. - Constant illumination may indicate a fault in the traction control system; service is recommended at an authorized Aventro Service Center. Maintenance & Service If you experience issues with traction control (warning lights, loss of system function), contact your nearest Aventro Service Center for diagnostics and repair. Problems could relate to faulty wheel speed sensors, wiring, or ECU malfunction. Related Services at Aventro Motors • Electrical System Diagnostics 2

• Dashboard Display Repair • Wheel Alignment • Regular Maintenance Frequently Asked Questions Can I switch off traction control? Some models offer the ability to temporarily disable traction control, useful in specific situations like getting a stuck vehicle moving. Refer to your Aventro Motors owner’s manual for guidance. Does traction control replace winter tires? No, traction control assists traction, but does not substitute proper tire selection for icy or snowy conditions. For further information, service, or support, contact Aventro Motors Service Centers or email info@aventromotors.com. 3

What is ABS (Anti-lock Braking System) and How Does It Work? Introduction ABS stands for Anti-lock Braking System. It is a vital safety feature in mod- ern vehicles, designed to prevent the wheels from locking up during emergency braking situations. By maintaining tractive contact with the road surface, ABS enhances vehicle control and reduces stopping distances on both wet and dry surfaces. Key Purpose of ABS • Prevents wheel lock-up during sudden or hard braking. • Maintains steering control, allowing the driver to maneuver the vehicle while braking. • Reduces the risk of skidding or uncontrolled vehicle movement. How Does ABS Work? ABS operates using a combination of sensors, valves, and electronic control units. Here is a simplified step-by-step process: 1. Wheel Speed Sensors • ABS uses sensors located at each wheel to monitor the rotational speed of the wheels continuously. • If any sensor detects a sudden decrease in wheel speed (indicating potential lock-up), the ABS system is activated. 2. Electronic Control Unit (ECU) • The ECU receives data from the wheel speed sensors. • When it detects a wheel about to lock, it controls the hydraulic brake pressure through a modulator. 3. 1

Hydraulic Valves/Modulator • These valves rapidly increase or decrease brake pressure to each wheel as needed. • This process occurs many times per second (often felt as a “pulsating” brake pedal). 4. Brake Release and Reapplication • By releasing and then reapplying the brakes repeatedly in quick suc- cession, ABS prevents the wheels from locking up. • The driver can continue to steer effectively even during heavy brak- ing. Advantages of ABS • Improved Steering Control: Allows the driver to steer around obsta- cles while braking hard. • Shorter Stopping Distance: Especially on slippery or wet roads, ABS can reduce stopping distances. • Reduced Tire Wear: Prevents flat-spotting of tires due to skidding. When is ABS Most Useful? • Wet or icy roads • Gravel or loose road surfaces • Emergency stops requiring both braking and steering maneuvers Common Misconceptions • ABS does not decrease stopping distance in all conditions, es- pecially on loose gravel or snow where locked wheels can help build up material in front of the tires. • ABS is not a substitute for safe driving or maintaining a safe follow- ing distance. How ABS Feels in Action • During hard braking, you may feel a pulsating sensation in the brake pedal. 2

• This is normal and indicates that the ABS is actively working. • Do not pump the brakes; instead, apply firm, continuous pressure. Conclusion Anti-lock Braking System (ABS) is a critical automotive safety technology that saves lives by helping drivers maintain control of their vehicles in emer- gency situations. By understanding how ABS works, drivers can maximize its benefits and contribute to safer roads. References: - NHTSA - Anti-lock Braking Systems - How Stuff Works - How ABS Works 3
